items.name: Heather-and-Honey Hillside Tea
items.effect: A dozen twists of dried heather, honeycomb and marshmallow root that brew into a sweet, throat-soothing tea. A cup during a short rest gives advantage on your next Constitution check or save against a cough, chill or ordinary cold-weather illness.

recipe.lore: Shepherds swear by it: heather for warmth, honey to carry it, and marshmallow root to coat a raw throat after a night on the fells.

items.name: Samphire Sailor's Pickle
items.effect: A crock of briny samphire and sea lettuce that keeps for months. A week of it alongside ordinary rations prevents scurvy and the slow sickness of long voyages, and it counts as a day's food per jar.

recipe.lore: Tidal-flat greens are the old deckhand's cure; salt and vinegar keep them crisp long after the coast is out of sight.

items.name: Woad Warrior's Paint
items.effect: A pot of fermented woad fixed with alum and tallow, enough for five applications. Painted in swirling blue, you gain advantage on the first Intimidation check you make before the paint is washed off (lasts until your next long rest).

recipe.lore: Woad stinks while it ferments and stains for days — alum fixes the colour so it doesn't run with sweat or rain, which is the point when you want to look like a ghost from the moors.

items.name: Marchwarden Yew Longbow
items.effect: A carefully seasoned longbow cut from the boundary between yew heartwood and sapwood. Its normal range is 20 feet longer than a standard longbow's.

recipe.lore: Heartwood resists compression and sapwood stretches — a stave that keeps both is a bow that throws further. Flax whipping and beeswax guard it against damp.

items.name: Scrapmonger's Brigandine
items.effect: Studded leather riveted together from bandit leathers, torn mail and flattened arrowheads, with brass knuckle-plates in the gauntlets. It works as studded leather armour but weighs 5 pounds more and gives disadvantage on Stealth checks; while wearing it your unarmed strikes deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage.

recipe.lore: Every bandit camp is an armoury in pieces. Straps become the jack, notched steel the plates, arrowheads are hammered flat into rivets, and a thug's brass knuckles are sewn into the gauntlets.

items.name: Bone-Plank Marsh Buckler
items.effect: A shield of salvaged boards reinforced with lizardfolk bone ribs and a bone spearhead boss. It works as a normal shield, but contains no metal: it can't rust, conduct lightning or be heated by magic.

recipe.lore: Lizardfolk build without iron because iron rots in the swamp; their bone and boards survive where a knight's shield would be flaking orange in a month.

items.name: Scavenger's Scrap Caltrops
items.effect: A bag of twenty caltrops hammered from pitted grave-iron, ooze-etched buckles and oddments out of an ogre's sack. They work as caltrops, and a creature that takes damage from them also can't take the Dash action until the start of its next turn.

recipe.lore: Metal that has sat in a cube is already pitted into jagged points, grave-iron snaps sharp, and a grimlock's stone spikes knock free whole. Nothing from a scrap heap goes to waste.

items.name: Giant-Sack Patchwork Tent
items.effect: A four-person tent stitched from a hill giant's hide sack and ogre wraps. It still reeks faintly of giant: ordinary beasts with keen smell avoid approaching within 30 feet of it unless starving or provoked.

recipe.lore: No wolf wants to wander into a giant's larder. The hides are re-tanned in mangrove bark so they stop rotting, but the old smell does more guarding than any watch rota.

items.name: Crofter's Heather Pipe
items.effect: A mended clay pipe and a pouch of heather-and-birch blend. Its smoke keeps midges, mosquitoes and ticks away: while it's smoked at camp, the group has advantage on saves against insect-borne disease that night.

recipe.lore: Every crofter's pocket holds a pipe and a knife. Birch smoke and heather drive off the biting flies that bring marsh fever.

items.name: Boiled-Rag Field Dressings
items.effect: A roll of boiled rags treated with alum and spirits, with a pot of marshmallow-root poultice. It holds 5 uses; each use lets you stabilize a creature as a healer's kit does, and the treated creature has advantage on its next save against infection or disease from the wound.

recipe.lore: Rags boiled in spirits are cleaner than a fine shirt; alum closes small bleeds, cattail down packs a wound, and marshmallow root draws out the heat of a festering cut.

items.name: Scout's Folding Spyglass
items.effect: A compact collapsing spyglass built around a flawless salvaged lens. It works as a spyglass but folds to pocket size, and its lens doesn't fog in cold or damp.

recipe.lore: Grinding a lens is most of a spyglass's cost; a scout's lens is already perfect, needing only a new body.

items.name: Mephit-Slag Bedwarmer
items.effect: A clay-wrapped lump of magma mephit slag that stays pleasantly warm for 8 hours after being held for a minute. Kept in your bedroll, it counts as cold-weather gear, and it never grows hot enough to burn.

recipe.lore: Mephit slag is still half-alive with the heat of the Plane of Fire; clay tames it so it only warms and never scorches.

items.name: Shard-Saint Reliquary Charm
items.effect: A silver locket enclosing a fragment of a broken holy symbol. It serves as a holy symbol, and when you use it to stabilize a dying creature, that creature also regains 1 hit point. Works once per dawn.

recipe.lore: A shattered holy symbol still remembers its prayers; set in silver with the beads that carried them and a chip of moon-bright selenite, it gives a little of that grace to the wounded.

items.name: Goblin's Lucky Rat Skull
items.effect: A grinning rat skull on a string of bottle caps and a pressed four-leaf clover. Once per dawn, when you roll a 1 on an ability check, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

recipe.lore: Goblins believe their junk is lucky; nobody believed them until a clover was sewn into the jaw, and the rolls started coming up.

items.name: Desert-Rose Dust Brooch
items.effect: A brooch of rosette gypsum crystals rinsed in mephit grit. While wearing it, blowing sand, dust clouds and similar particulate can't blind you, and sand never gets into your eyes, food or boots.

recipe.lore: Desert roses grow out of the sand itself, so the sand respects them; a pinch of mephit grit teaches the charm what to push away. Old coin makes a cheap gold setting.

items.name: Red-Coral Drowning Ward
items.effect: A polished branch of blood-red coral strung on silver wire. You can hold your breath for twice as long as normal, and if you fall unconscious in water you float face-up.

recipe.lore: Fisher-wives hang red coral on their husbands against drowning; the sea recognises its own blood and gives the wearer back.

items.name: Floating Glowcrystal Lamp
items.effect: A small cage lamp holding a cave glowcrystal and fitted with homunculus wings. It sheds bright light in 20 feet and dim light for 20 more, and on command it hovers and follows 5 feet behind you. It can't carry anything and falls if struck.

recipe.lore: The glowcrystal needs no oil and gives no heat, and a homunculus's wings were made to hover by their master's shoulder — they are happy to do so again.

items.name: Rimefog Flask
items.effect: An essence vessel holding a captured ice mephit core. Unstopper it as an action and it releases a freezing fog in a 15-foot-radius sphere that heavily obscures the area for 1 minute and frosts every surface in it.

recipe.lore: Ice mephits vanish into their own fog to ambush travellers; kept alive in the vessel, the core does it once more when released.

items.name: Icebloom Rime Oil
items.effect: A pale oil that frosts a weapon white. For 1 hour, the coated weapon deals an extra 1d4 cold damage on a hit, and a creature hit by it has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

recipe.lore: Icebloom petals never thaw; pressed into oil with slow-melting mephit ice, they pass that frost to anything they touch.

items.name: Sandman's Dustpouch
items.effect: A pouch of golden, yawning dust. As an action, blow it at a creature within 5 feet: it must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or fall asleep for 1 minute (waking if it takes damage or is shaken). Creatures with more than 20 hit points are unaffected.

recipe.lore: A dust mephit's core makes anyone who stares at it yawn; crushed with dreamcap and heather, it turns a yawn into a nap.

items.name: Wailing Puffball Thunderpod
items.effect: A lacquered puffball that screams when it bursts. Throw it up to 30 feet: each creature within 10 feet of impact must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or be deafened for 1 minute, and the shriek is heard up to a mile away.

recipe.lore: The puffball screams on its own; a coat of pitch keeps it from going off in your pack, and a wool wadding makes the crack louder when it does.

items.name: Magmin Firesand Grenade
items.effect: A clay shell of volcanic sand and magmin crust. Thrown up to 30 feet, it bursts in a 5-foot radius: creatures there take 1d6 fire damage (DC 11 Dexterity save for none), and the glittering sand sheds dim light in the area for 1 minute.

recipe.lore: Magmin crust ignites at a spark; volcanic sand holds the heat and keeps glowing after the flash, which the fire-watch calls a gift and thieves call a nuisance.

items.name: Magmin Sparkheart Tinderbox
items.effect: A brass tinderbox with a living magmin spark sealed in its lid. Opening it lights a torch, candle, lamp or campfire as a bonus action, even in rain, and it can warm a pot of water to boiling in a minute.

recipe.lore: A magmin core tries to light anything it touches, which makes it a terrible pet and a perfect tinderbox.

items.name: Steamveil Brooch
items.effect: A copper brooch with a bead of shimmering vapour behind glass. Once per dawn, as a reaction when a creature you can see attacks you, you vanish in a puff of steam; the attack roll has disadvantage.

recipe.lore: Steam mephits blur the air around them; a bead of their core sealed over a few everboiling scald-drops can still exhale that veil at the right moment.

items.name: Svirfneblin Rockshade Hood
items.effect: A mottled grey hood and mantle sewn around a gargoyle heartstone. While you remain motionless against rock, you look like part of it: creatures have disadvantage on Perception checks to notice you unless they touch you.

recipe.lore: Deep gnomes weave the stone into their cloaks; a gargoyle's heartstone, which looks exactly like rubble, sits at the nape and convinces watchers there is nothing there but rock.

items.name: Hovering-Hilt Dagger
items.effect: A dagger re-hilted from a flying sword's blade with its hover-rune in the pommel. When you let go of it, you can make it hang motionless in the air where you released it for up to 1 hour; you can pluck it back as part of any action.

recipe.lore: A flying sword's blade still twitches upward in the hand; the rune that lifted it is happy to keep it aloft if you ask politely.

items.name: Animus-Rune Armour Buckle
items.effect: A steel buckle etched with the rune that once animated a suit of armour. Fixed to a set of armour, it lets the armour buckle and unbuckle itself: donning or doffing it takes only an action, whatever its type.

recipe.lore: The rune once made empty plate walk; now it only makes plate step onto its wearer. Barding scrap gives it the familiar feel of armour to bind to.

items.name: Bugbear Snatch-Sack
items.effect: A muffling sack lined with rug-of-smothering yarn. On command its drawstring cinches itself tight, and nothing inside can be heard beyond 5 feet — clinking loot, a ticking device or a gagged prisoner.

recipe.lore: Bugbears bag their victims in silence; a rug of smothering strangles them the same way. Put the two together and nothing gets out, not even a sound.

items.name: Legion Drill Pennant
items.effect: A hobgoblin legion standard cut down to a spear pennant. Once per dawn, as an action, raise it: one frightened ally within 30 feet who can see it may immediately repeat the save to end the effect.

recipe.lore: Hobgoblin soldiers fear losing the banner more than death; flown over your own line, it steadies the nerve of anyone drilled to follow a standard.

items.name: Kobold Ember-Idol
items.effect: A palm-sized dragon idol whose mouth glows like banked coals. Once per dawn, you can make it breathe a thread of flame that lights a candle, torch or campfire within 5 feet, and your hands stay warm while you hold it.

recipe.lore: Kobolds blacken their idols with countless offerings; soak one in lamp-oil and seat a flake of lava in the jaws, and the little dragon finally answers.

items.name: Old Soldier's Luck Medal
items.effect: A campaign medal polished and restrung on a red ribbon. Once per dawn, when you fail a saving throw against being frightened, you can reroll it and must use the new roll.

recipe.lore: Veterans swear the medal is lucky because the one who wore it lived to earn it. Coin from the same purse re-silvers its face.

items.name: Crowd-Pleaser's Shield
items.effect: A shield fitted with a champion's polished boss. Whenever a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can make the boss ring out like a gong (heard 300 feet away), and you have advantage on your next Performance check before the end of the fight.

components.label: A fighter's trophy of renown (champion's shield boss, campaign medal or heraldic plate)

recipe.lore: Arena crowds cheer the block as much as the kill; a champion's boss still remembers the roar and wants to hear it again. A veteran's campaign medal or a knight's heraldic plate remembers its own cheering crowds.

items.name: Desecrated Athame
items.effect: A cult's ritual dagger rebound around a smashed idol. Once per dawn, when you hit a creature with it, the creature can't regain hit points until the start of your next turn.

recipe.lore: The idol's malice doesn't leave when the cult does; ground into the hilt, it lets the knife carry a small, stingy curse.

items.name: Gossamer Shriek-Tripwire
items.effect: A fine black wire with a shrieker cap sealed in a pouch at one end. Strung across a path (DC 15 Perception to spot), it shrieks for 1 minute when touched, loud enough to be heard 300 feet away.

components.label: Fine, near-invisible line (garrote wire, silver wire or ettercap silk)

recipe.lore: An assassin's wire is made not to be seen; a shrieker cap is made to scream when disturbed. Together they turn a killer's tool into a sentry. Any line thin enough to miss in the dark works: jeweller's silver wire or a strand of ettercap silk serve as well as a killer's garrote.

items.name: Tireless Charger Horseshoes
items.effect: Four horseshoes forged from skeletal barding with warhorse hoof-bone set into the nails. A mount wearing them can travel for 12 hours before needing to check for exhaustion from a forced march, and its hooves never split or go lame.

recipe.lore: A skeletal warhorse never tires because it has nothing left to tire. A little of that is hammered into the shoes of a living horse.

items.name: Gravebait Lure
items.effect: A sealed pot of twitching grave-flesh. Opened, it draws mindless undead: zombies and skeletons within 60 feet that fail a DC 11 Wisdom save move toward the pot and spend 1 minute worrying at it instead of attacking.

recipe.lore: Zombies are drawn to dead flesh that still twitches, as if calling to kin. Gutter cap is the rat-catcher's bait; it works as well on the dead as on rats.

items.name: Trollspur Buckler
items.effect: A shield bristling with troll claws lashed on with undying zombie sinew. Its spikes regrow and chipped wood knits overnight, and a creature that grapples you takes 1d4 piercing damage at the start of each of its turns.

components.label: Self-mending tissue (troll claws, budding ochre jelly or wererat blood)

recipe.lore: Troll claws keep growing after they're cut; sinew that refuses to stay severed keeps them lashed on. The shield repairs itself because nothing in it knows how to stay broken. Hedge-smiths without a troll use budding ochre jelly or a soak of wererat blood; the wood still refuses to stay broken, though the spikes are plain iron.

items.name: Graveshaft Longbow
items.effect: A yew longbow strung with the sinew of an ogre zombie. The string can't be cut, snapped or slackened by weather, and you can leave the bow strung indefinitely without it losing its cast. When you are knocked unconscious, you never drop it.

recipe.lore: An ogre zombie's tendons keep pulling long after death. As a bowstring they never tire; as a grip, they never let go.

items.name: Duskglass Goggles
items.effect: Smoked goggles fogged with a shadow's essence. While wearing them you see in dim light within 30 feet as if it were bright light, but they give no sight in total darkness.

recipe.lore: A shadow lives in the half-light; its essence bottled in glass smoked with its own residue turns the dusk into its home, and yours.

items.name: Specter-Wisp Snuffer Ring
items.effect: A cold pewter ring with a grey wisp in its stone. Once per dawn, as an action, you can extinguish every nonmagical flame within 20 feet of you.

recipe.lore: A specter is so hungry for life that flames gutter as it passes; caught in a ring, its hunger can be pointed at the candles.

items.name: Grave-Warden's Salve
items.effect: A grey balm of ghast marrow-dust cut with holy water and marshmallow root. Rubbed on your skin, it grants advantage on saves against paralysis caused by undead for 1 hour.

recipe.lore: Like against like: the ghast's own dust, sanctified, teaches your flesh to shrug off its touch.

items.name: Ghoulgrip Toxin
items.effect: A yellow film scraped from ghast claws. Applied to a weapon or ammunition (one dose lasts 1 minute), a creature hit must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or its speed drops to 0 until the end of its next turn.

recipe.lore: A ghast's paralytic film is strong enough to stiffen an elf; thinned and fixed, it only locks the legs, which is usually enough.

items.name: Violet Rot Paste
items.effect: A purple, carrion-smelling paste of fungus tendril and rotbloom. Applied to a weapon, the next creature hit within 1 minute takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage and can't regain hit points until the end of its next turn.

recipe.lore: Violet fungus rots flesh at a touch and rotbloom spreads wasting sickness; together the wound festers before it can close.

items.name: Homunculus Slumber Venom
items.effect: One dose of clear, sweet venom. A creature hit by a coated weapon must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 minute; if it fails by 5 or more, it also falls unconscious until it takes damage or someone uses an action to wake it.

recipe.lore: A homunculus's bite sends victims into dreamless sleep; dreamcap gives that sleep a little more weight.

items.name: Wererat Squeeze-Charm
items.effect: A long yellow incisor wrapped in greasy thread. Once per dawn, for 1 minute, you can squeeze through spaces as if you were one size smaller without penalty.

recipe.lore: The incisor is shed in the moment of changing back from rat to person; it still remembers being small enough for a drainpipe. Gutter cap keeps the sewer smell that makes the charm work.

items.name: Rustletwig Ghillie Wrap
items.effect: A mantle woven with living twigs from an awakened shrub. While motionless in foliage, you look like an ordinary bush, and the twigs rustle quietly to warn you — you can't be surprised by a creature that moves through the undergrowth within 10 feet.

recipe.lore: Awakened shrubs hide by standing still among ordinary ones; their twigs still rustle when something draws near, as if gossiping.

items.name: Heartwood Memory Staff
items.effect: A druidic focus carved from an awakened tree's heartwood. Once per dawn, press it to a living tree to learn what Small or larger creatures passed within 30 feet of that tree in the last hour.

recipe.lore: Heartwood keeps rings of memory; one that once thought for itself can still listen to another tree's.

items.name: Blackthorn Hexing Cane
items.effect: A twisted blackthorn walking stick. Once per dawn, as an action, point it at a creature within 30 feet and mutter a curse: it must succeed on a DC 11 Wisdom save or subtract 1d4 from the next attack roll it makes within 1 minute.

recipe.lore: Blackthorn twists as it grows, and witches say it grows around a grudge. A rotbloom rubbed into the grain gives it something to hate.

items.name: Hedge-Mage's Primer
items.effect: A thick primer of salvaged folios, vermilion rubrics and pressed spell components. A wizard may copy two 1st-level spells from it. Anyone can read one page as an action to cast prestidigitation, once per dawn.

components.label: Pressed arcane reagent (component pouch, spell residue or homunculus blood)

recipe.lore: A dead mage's component pouch holds half the spells he knew in dried form; pressed between pages and labelled in cinnabar red, it teaches a patient reader the rest. Without a dead mage's pouch, residue scraped from an old casting circle or a drop of a familiar's blood gives the rubrics their spark.

items.name: Shardlight Wand
items.effect: A wand tipped with a chip of a broken arcane focus. It has 3 charges; expend one to cast light or dancing lights. It regains 1d3 charges at dawn.

components.label: Small arcane spark (focus shard, deepglow lichen or an animus rune)

recipe.lore: A shattered focus still gathers a trickle of power; a glowcrystal gives that trickle an easy thing to do. Deepglow lichen or the chipped rune of an animated armour hold the same small trickle of power as a broken focus.

items.name: Gemscent Prospector's Ring
items.effect: A rough-cut gem ring bound with xorn gut. While attuned, you can smell precious metals and gems within 60 feet, even through stone, and once per dawn you can cast locate object, seeking only a metal or gemstone object.

recipe.lore: A xorn smells treasure through solid rock and swims to it; its gizzard remembers every stone it ground. Deep gnome gems give the ring something to look for.

items.name: Frost-Giant Wintermantle
items.effect: A heavy mantle cut from a frost giant's mammoth-fur cloak. You're comfortable in temperatures as low as -50 degrees Fahrenheit and automatically succeed on saves against extreme cold, and ice and snow don't slow you.

components.label: Deep-cold fur (a frost giant's mammoth cloak, mammoth wool or a polar bear pelt)

recipe.lore: Frost giants wear these cloaks through glacier storms; even cut down to human size, the fur remembers its master's indifference to cold. Northern trappers make a humbler version from raw mammoth wool or a polar bear's pelt.

items.name: Rime-Iron Bearded Axe
items.effect: A handaxe quenched in undying rime, forever beaded with frost. It deals an extra 1d4 cold damage on a hit, and once per turn a creature you hit has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. You're unharmed by holding it bare-handed.

recipe.lore: Frost giant iron, rime crystal or a winter wolf's fang never loses its chill; quenched again in mephit ice and gripped with polar-bear hide, the axe bites both ways and you're spared the frostbite.

items.name: Emberline Shortsword
items.effect: A shortsword reforged around a sliver of ever-hot fire, a glowing temper line running its length. On command it sheds torchlight, can deal fire damage instead of piercing, and once per dawn a hit deals an extra 2d6 fire damage.

recipe.lore: Fire giant steel keeps the heat of the forge in its heart; quenched in hot volcanic sand instead of water, the temper line never cools. Smiths who can't reach a giant's hall fold in an everburning cinder or a hell hound's fang instead.

items.name: Nightmare-Edge Glaive
items.effect: A glaive whose blade is an oni's reforged edge or steel quenched in bearded-devil ichor, blackened with umbral soot. Once per dawn, when you hit with it, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom save or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. It counts as magical against resistance.

recipe.lore: An oni's blade has cut many sleepers in their beds; blackened with shadow soot, it wears the shape of their nightmares.

items.name: Salamander-Coil Lash
items.effect: A whip braided from a salamander's tail. Once per turn when you hit a Large or smaller creature, you can try to wrap it: it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or be grappled (escape DC 13), taking 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns while wrapped.

recipe.lore: A salamander's tail coils and tightens around its prey while it burns; braided, the muscle never forgets the habit.

items.name: Pilgrim's Silver Reliquary
items.attune: by a cleric, druid, paladin or ranger
items.effect: A silver case enclosing a saint's relic. It has 3 charges; expend 1 to cast cure wounds (1st level) or protection from evil and good. Regains 1d3 charges at dawn.

recipe.lore: A priest's relic has absorbed a lifetime of healing prayers; rehoused in silver beside a fragment of another holy symbol, it answers pilgrims as it answered its keeper.

items.name: Counter-Pact Scroll
items.effect: A vellum scroll written over a fiend's torn pact page. Reading it casts remove curse; if the target is bound by a fiendish pact, the patron can't sense or scry on it for the next 24 hours.

recipe.lore: Every pact has a mirror clause. Written backwards over the fiend's own signature in blessed ink, the scroll reads as a revocation.

items.name: Oath-Bound Heraldic Breastplate
items.effect: A breastplate reworked from a knight's enamelled heraldic plate. Once per dawn, when an ally within 5 feet is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to take the damage instead.

recipe.lore: The knight swore to shield others; the enamel still carries the oath. A campaign medal riveted under the gorget reminds it who it serves now.

items.name: Cinder-Studded Jack
items.effect: Studded leather refitted with a half-dragon veteran's scale-studded panels. Once per dawn, as a reaction when you take fire damage, you gain resistance to fire until the end of the turn.

recipe.lore: Red scales shed by a half-dragon were never scorched in a hundred fights; the panels pass that disdain for flame to whoever wears them.

items.name: Moonhunter's Talisman
items.effect: A werewolf's moon-touched claw bound in silver. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell, and once per dawn you can cast hunter's mark without a spell slot.

recipe.lore: The claw stays wolfish after the body reverts, silvered under the moon. Selenite and silver keep the curse tame while the hunter's senses leak through.

items.name: Tusk of the Relentless Boar
items.effect: A curved wereboar tusk bound with undying ogre sinew. Once per long rest, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you drop to 1 hit point instead.

recipe.lore: A wereboar keeps fighting after wounds that should have dropped it; bound with tendons that refuse to stay dead, the tusk shares that stubbornness.

items.name: Striped Pounce Anklet
items.effect: An anklet set with a weretiger's striped claw. Once per turn, if you move at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and then hit it with a melee attack on the same turn, it must succeed on a DC 13 Strength save or be knocked prone. You also have advantage on Stealth checks in tall grass.

recipe.lore: The claw is shed at the instant of change, still curved for the pounce. Tiger-gold dye on the beads makes the grass forget you.

items.name: Bearward Bracers
items.effect: Leather bracers studded with a werebear's broad claw. Your carrying capacity doubles and you have advantage on Strength checks to grapple or shove; once per dawn, as a bonus action, you gain 2d6 temporary hit points.

recipe.lore: Werebears are the gentlest of the moon-cursed and the most protective; druids say their shed claws still want to stand between you and harm.

items.name: Mourning Ghostlight Locket
items.effect: A ghost's anchoring keepsake reset in a silver locket. Once per dawn, as an action, you can see invisible creatures and into the Ethereal Plane within 30 feet for 1 minute; ghosts you see this way know you can see them.

recipe.lore: The keepsake held a ghost to this world, so it knows the way across. A glowcrystal lights the path for your eyes.

items.name: Gravebinder's Circle Chalk
items.effect: A stick of chalk kneaded with vampire coffin-earth. Drawing a 10-foot circle takes 1 minute; for 1 hour, an undead creature of CR 3 or lower inside it can't willingly leave. It can attempt a DC 13 Charisma save at the end of each of its turns to break free.

components.label: Grave-soil of a bound undead (vampire coffin-earth or wight barrow-dust)

recipe.lore: A vampire is bound to the soil of its grave; chalk mixed with that soil draws a grave around any lesser undead. Dust from a wight's barrow is grave-soil too, and binds nearly as well.

items.name: Blood-Sipping Stiletto
items.effect: A slender dagger set with a vampire spawn's fang. Once per dawn, when you hit with it, the target takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage and you regain hit points equal to that amount.

recipe.lore: A spawn's fang still wants to drink; set into steel, it sips and passes the stolen vigour back up the hilt.

items.name: Barrow Signet of Command
items.effect: A cold iron signet holding a wight's spiteful ember. It has 3 charges; expend 1 to cast command (save DC 13) on an undead creature. Regains 1d3 charges at dawn.

recipe.lore: A wight commands the corpses it raises; its essence, set in grave-iron and dusted with a ghast's grave-dirt, lends its voice to yours.

items.name: Reforged Barrow-Blade
items.effect: A longsword reforged from a barrow-king's pitted blade. It deals an extra 1d4 necrotic damage on a hit, and a creature slain by it can't be raised as undead.

recipe.lore: Barrow steel has drunk the cold of the grave for centuries; reforged with a bog-oak grip, it carries death but keeps the dead where they fall.

items.name: Pudding-Graft Draught
items.effect: A black, slowly dividing tonic. When you drink it you regain 2d4 + 2 hit points, then regain 2 more at the start of each of your turns for the next 5 rounds; the regrowth stops if you drop to 0 hit points.

recipe.lore: Black pudding never stops dividing; tamed with an ochre bud as a starter, the jelly splits into new flesh instead of eating it.

items.name: Galvanic Rot-Heart Totem
items.effect: A knot of rotting roots bound in copper wire. Once per dawn, as a reaction when you would take lightning damage, you take none and instead gain temporary hit points equal to the damage (maximum 20).

recipe.lore: A shambling mound grows fat on lightning strikes; its rot-heart, wired in copper, still drinks the current before it can hurt you.

items.name: Stoneward Talisman
items.effect: A disc of banded petrified wood. You have advantage on saves against being petrified. Once per dawn, as a reaction when you are hit by an attack, your skin takes on the grain of stone: you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage until the end of the turn.

recipe.lore: Petrified wood is a living thing that became stone and still keeps its rings; it teaches your skin to do the same for a heartbeat, and then to come back.

items.name: Peat-Black Cudgel
items.effect: A club carved from ancient bog oak, black as jet and nearly unbreakable. It counts as magical, can't be broken by non-magical means, and deals an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage to undead.

recipe.lore: Bog oak has lain with the dead for thousands of years and fears nothing about them. Salt worked into the grain stings anything that ought to be buried.

items.name: Darkwood Buckler
items.effect: A +1 shield of charcoal-grey darkwood that weighs only 2 pounds. You can don or doff it as a bonus action.

recipe.lore: Darkwood is as light as balsa but as strong as oak; a shield of it moves as fast as your arm does, and turns blows as well as steel.

items.name: Mason's Living-Stone Trowel
items.effect: A trowel with a blade of earth-elemental living stone. Stonework you repair with it slowly knits itself for a week afterwards. Once per dawn, you can use it to cast stone shape.

recipe.lore: Living stone knits its own cracks; worked into lime and clay, it teaches mortar to do the same, and the blade remembers how to move rock like water. The keystone must be true living stone from the Plane of Earth or a stone giant's heartstone; an earth elemental's lesser stone only steadies the blade.

items.name: Ravings-Cap Augur's Tincture
items.effect: A whispering violet tincture. Drinking it lets you cast augury, the visions coming in the words of someone else. Afterward, roll a d6: on a 1, you babble nonsense and can't speak coherently for 1 minute.

recipe.lore: Ravings cap whispers as it dries — seers say it is repeating what the future told it. Dreamcap softens the babble, spirits carry it, and sometimes it isn't quite enough.

items.name: Dreamslate of the Stone-Sleepers
items.effect: A trance-carved slate tablet. Once per dawn, after a long rest with your head upon it, you can cast divination. Once per dawn, you can also cast meld into stone.

recipe.lore: Stone giants dream when they come to the surface world and carve what they see; recut and anointed with dreamcap, the slate lets another sleeper dream the giant's truths.

items.name: Pharaoh's Canopic Periapt
items.effect: A gold-wrapped periapt around a mummy lord's preserved heart. You have resistance to necrotic damage and your hit point maximum can't be reduced. Once per dawn, when you drop to 0 hit points, you instead rise at the start of your next turn with half your hit points — but you have vulnerability to fire until your next long rest.

recipe.lore: A mummy lord cannot be destroyed while its heart survives; wrapped in the pharaoh's own burial gold-linen, it keeps a sliver of that refusal for the wearer — along with its old fear of fire.

items.name: Scavenger's Climbing Rig
items.effect: Fifty feet of re-laid rope with a grapnel, ten heavy giant-iron pitons and a pair of talon-tipped hand picks. It counts as rope, grapnel and climber's kit; the hooks and pitons hold in ice, frozen soil and cracked stone, and you have advantage on Athletics checks to climb stone.

components.label: Hooked talons for the hand picks

recipe.lore: Old rope is only weak where it frays, so it is unlaid and spliced with fresh flax. An ettin's spiked iron is dense enough to draw into pitons that bite where normal iron bends, and a gargoyle's stone claw finds a grip in mortar that would shatter a steel pick. Where no gargoyle is to be had, a blood hawk's hooked talons, set in hardwood grips, bite nearly as well into ice and mortar.

items.name: Mazerunner's Horn-and-Skull Charm
items.effect: A carved wedge of minotaur horn with a skull chip swinging in a brass socket. The chip always points toward the way you entered the building, cave or dungeon you are inside, and you have advantage on Strength checks to break down doors and barricades.

recipe.lore: A minotaur's skull never forgets the way out of its maze, and its horn remembers every wall it charged through. Between them, no labyrinth holds you for long.

items.name: Warband Bone Horn
items.effect: A horn hung with a gnoll's bone fetish and a scrap of orc war-totem. When you blow it, a cackling howl carries a mile; beasts of Intelligence 3 or lower within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom save or flee from you for 1 minute. Once per dawn.

recipe.lore: Gnolls hunt with laughter and orcs charge behind their totems; animals learned to run from both sounds long before people did.

items.name: Smuggler's Papers
items.effect: A leather wallet holding a cartographer's clean copy of a bandit map and a forged watch warrant backed by a genuine badge. You have advantage on Survival checks to navigate the charted region and know 1d4 of its hidden caches, and on Deception checks to pass as a watch officer where nobody knows the local watch.

recipe.lore: Bandits draw maps for themselves and nobody else; a real badge sells a forged writ better than any signature. Both come off the same kind of corpse.
